With production ending in 2022, it is the last Learjet model. ==Design== [[File:N577LJ Learjet 75 cabin.jpg|thumb|The flat-floor cabin is {{cvt|1.50|by|1.55|m|ft|order=flip}} wide and high.]] [[File:Learjet 75 on static display, EBACE 2018, Le Grand-Saconnex (BL7C0612).jpg|thumb|Learjet 75 left side, with the door open]] These models feature new avionics, [[winglet]]s, and powerful engines that use less fuel.{{cite news |author= Ross Marowits |publisher= The Canadian Press |url= http://www.canadianbusiness.com/business-news/bombardier-preparing-for-light-business-aircraft-recovery-with-learjet-upgrades/ |title= Bombardier preparing for light business aircraft recovery with Learjet upgrades |work= Canadian Business |date= May 14, 2012 |archive-date= October 10, 2017 |access-date= June 6, 2017 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20171010005439/http://www.canadianbusiness.com/business-news/bombardier-preparing-for-light-business-aircraft-recovery-with-learjet-upgrades/ |url-status= dead }} The [[Learjet 40]]/[[Learjet 45|45]] light jet is updated with touchscreen-controlled [[Garmin G3000|Garmin G5000]] avionics and a modern interior. The combination of aerodynamic improvements, which lowered the design's drag by 2%, and 200 lbs less weight in the nose section resulted in an increased range of 4%.{{cite news |url= http://aviationweek.com/business-aviation/operators-survey-bombardier-learjet-7075 |title= Operators Survey: Bombardier Learjet 70/75 |date= Mar 28, 2017 |author= Fred George |work= Business & Commercial Aviation |publisher= Aviation Week}} The canted winglet design was incorporated from the [[Bombardier Global 7500]]/8000.{{cite news |url= http://aviationweek.com/business-aviation/bombardier-unveils-learjet-70-and-75 |magazine= Aviation Week Network |date= 14 May 2012 |title= Bombardier Unveils Learjet 70 and 75 |author= Fred George}} Both variants are powered by {{cvt|3,850|lbf|kN}} [[Honeywell TFE731]]-40BR turbofans with [[thrust reverser]]s, have a [[maximum takeoff weight|MTOW]] of {{cvt|21,500|lb}} and a fuel capacity of {{cvt|6,062|lb}} for a maximum range of {{cvt|2,050|nmi|mi km}} with four passengers. Typical cruise is Mach .76 and high-speed cruise is Mach .79, the ceiling is [[Flight level|FL]]510 where the cabin altitude is {{cvt|8,000|ft}}. Their flat-floor cabin width is {{cvt|1.50|by|1.55|m|ftin|order=flip}} high, the Learjet 70's seven-seat cabin length is {{cvt|5.38|and|6.05|m|ftin|order=flip}} for the nine-seat, double-club Learjet 75. The forward galley facing the entry door is isolated by a [[pocket door]] from the seating area with a [[Lufthansa Technik]] cabin management, and the aft lavatory has a belted seat. The {{cvt|50|cuft}} external baggage hold is heated but not pressurized. At FL410, ISA + {{cvt|3|C-change|0}} and Mach .78 for {{cvt|462|kn|mph km/h}}, its hourly fuel burn is {{cvt|1000|lb}} and {{cvt|1400|lb}} at Mach .80. ==Development== Two of the planned five flight test aircraft, a modified Learjet 40XR and Learjet 45XR, had flown by July 2012.{{citation |last1=Fredericks |first1=Carey |title=Bombardier's Learjets on Track for 2013 Arrival |url=http://www.wingsmagazine.com/bombardiers-learjets-on-track-for-2013-arrival-7375 |access-date=7 November 2024 |work=Wings |date=11 July 2012}} The Learjet 75 received its type certificate from the FAA on 14 November 2013.{{cite news |url= http://www.kansas.com/news/business/aviation/article1127710.html |author= Molly McMillin |title= Bombardier's Learjet 75 gets FAA certification |date= November 15, 2013 |work= Wichita Eagle}} Deliveries began shortly thereafter.{{cite news |url= http://aviationweek.com/business-aviation/new-bizjets-advance-bombardier-looks-ahead |title= As New BizJets Advance, Bombardier Looks Ahead |date= 3 Dec 2013 |work= [[Aviation Week]] }}{{Dead link|date=September 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}{{efn|The "start of the delivery process" began on 17 October 2013.{{cite news |title=Learjet 75 Deliveries Begin |url=http://www.ainonline.com/aviation-news/business-aviation/2013-10-18/learjet-75-deliveries-begin |access-date=7 November 2024 |work=AIN |date=18 October 2013}}}} This delay in certification caused order cancellations, and Bombardier's overall deliveries fell below expectations.{{cite news |url= production of Learjet 70 had been temporarily discontinued due to lack of orders (with Learjet 75 still being produced at that time).{{Cite web|url=https://www.ainonline.com/aviation-news/business-aviation/2016-11-02/bombardier-wrestles-learjet-future|title=Bombardier Wrestles With Learjet Future|first=Mark|last=Huber|website=Aviation International News}} The 100th Learjet 75 was delivered in June 2017.{{cite press release |url= http://businessaircraft.bombardier.com/en/news-events/bombardier-marks-major-milestone-delivery-3000th-learjet-aircraft-manufactured |title= Bombardier Marks Major Milestone with Delivery of 3,000th Learjet Aircraft Manufactured |date= 2 Jun 2017 |publisher= Bombardier}} By January 2019, Bombardier had delivered 132 Learjet 40/40XRs, 454 45/45XRs, and nearly 130 70/75s, including 24 in 2016 and 14 in 2017.{{cite news |url= https://www.ainonline.com/aviation-news/business-aviation/2019-01-17/pilot-report-learjet-75 |title= Pilot Report: Learjet 75 |author= Matt Thurber |date= January 17, 2019 |work= AIN online}} In June, Bombardier launched the sub-$10 million Learjet 75 Liberty to compete with the [[Cessna CitationJet]] and [[Embraer Phenom 300]] from 2020, with six seats down from eight, no standard [[auxiliary power unit|APU]] or lavatory sink, but still Part 25 and not [[FAR Part 23]] certified, with a maximum payload of {{cvt|1,320|kg|order=flip}} and a range of {{cvt|2,080|nmi|mi km}}.{{cite news |url= https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/bombardier-revamps-learjet-75-with-six-passenger-lib-459417/ |title= Bombardier revamps Learjet 75 with six-passenger Liberty |date= 2 July 2019 |author= Dominic Perry |work= Flightglobal}} Bombardier announced the end of the production of Learjet aircraft by the end of 2021.{{cite web|url= https://www.cbc.ca/news/business/bombardier-cuts-jobs-ends-learjet-production-1.5909993|title= Bombardier lays off another 1,600 people, scraps Learjet program|access-date= 11 February 2021|last= 75 was manufactured in January 2022.{{Cite web|title=Last New Learjet 75 Hits Milestone On Way To Delivery {{!}} Aviation Week Network|url=https://aviationweek.com/business-aviation/aircraft-propulsion/last-new-learjet-75-hits-milestone-way-delivery|access-date=2022-01-21|website=aviationweek.com}} As Bombardier focuses on its larger Challenger and Global jets, it was delivered on 28 March 2022.{{cite news |url=
